terra.problem: The dough comparison doesn't work: half a batch is perfectly usable, so it doesn't illustrate a divided heart.
“Wrong people” says “wrong” about the baker's answer.
The passage doesn't say Samuel knew the Philistine rulers were coming.
“Not yet” suggests Samuel later leads the men out against the Philistines. The passage says the men of Israel charged out, not that Samuel led them.
“The ark stays put” claims it remained at Kiriath-jearim throughout the passage. The text doesn't state that.
“Not what they've said” rules out sins of speech, but the confession doesn't specify what sins they committed.
“Israel didn't have to swing first” asserts an order of fighting that the passage doesn't give.
“That's a short fight” gives the conflict a duration the text doesn't provide.
The text doesn't say what happens whenever someone passes the stone or that it reminds every passerby.
“A stone is hard to argue with” doesn't connect a recognizable comparison to what Samuel does with the stone.
Calling the Moabites a neighbor brings in a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
The line about wanting his own bed attributes a desire to Samuel that the text doesn't give or mark as a guess.
The passage says the ark remained at Kiriath-jearim for twenty years, but it doesn't establish that it wasn't in Ramah when Samuel returned there.
“No request, no summons” rules out a request the text simply doesn't mention.
The text says Samuel built the altar in Ramah, not at his home.
